question: A 58-year-old lifeguard develops squamous cell carcinoma of the skin on his forehead. Which of the following most likely preceded the development of this carcinoma?
analysis: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) of the skin often develops from precancerous lesions that have been exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, particularly in individuals with significant sun exposure, such as a lifeguard. A dry, scaly, hyperkeratotic papule is a description of actinic keratosis, which is a known precursor to SCC. Actinic keratosis presents as rough, scaly patches on sun-exposed areas of the skin, and can progress to squamous cell carcinoma if left untreated.
